issues.legal_issue: A revenue officer must apply tax dues against compensation payable when the governing recovery rule directs that the dues be realized by deduction from compensation.
material_facts: Tax was due from an intermediary whose estate had vested in the State.
Compensation was payable to the intermediary, and the High Court considered that compensation to be still due.
The applicable rule directed that the relevant dues be realized by deduction from compensation, while preserving the State’s right to recover by other means.
issues.conclusion: The Collector had no option to adjust the tax liability against compensation still due; the rule imposed a duty to make the adjustment.
issues.legal_principle: Section 6(d) of the U.P. Zamindari Abolition and Land Reforms Act, 1951, read with section 26 and Rule 8-A, required specified dues to be realized by deduction from compensation. The opening words preserving the State’s right to recover by other means did not make the deduction optional; they preserved alternative recovery if adjustment could not be made effective. No earlier cases were relied on.

rule.if: tax_recovery_adjustment_dispute and tax_dues_are_within_the_rule and compensation_is_still_due and the_recovery_rule_directs_deduction

predicates.tax_recovery_adjustment_dispute: The matter concerns recovery of tax dues from an intermediary in connection with compensation payable for an estate that vested in the State.
predicates.tax_dues_are_within_the_rule: The dues are of a kind that the governing recovery rule directs to be recovered through deduction from compensation.
predicates.compensation_is_still_due: Compensation remains payable to the person liable for the dues.
predicates.the_recovery_rule_directs_deduction: The governing recovery rule directs the revenue officer to realize the relevant dues by deducting them from compensation.
predicates.collector_must_adjust_dues_against_compe: The revenue officer is required to apply the relevant dues against compensation that remains payable.

issues.definition: When a tax-recovery dispute concerns dues covered by a rule directing deduction from compensation, and compensation remains payable, the revenue officer must apply the dues against it.

issues.legal_issue: Agricultural income tax assessed after vesting qualifies for deduction from compensation when the tax is imposed on income earned during a previous year that ended before vesting.
material_facts: The tax assessment was made after the estate vested in the State.
The tax was imposed on agricultural income earned in the previous year, which ended before the date of vesting.
The intermediary sought adjustment of the tax liability against compensation.
issues.conclusion: The tax was for a period before vesting, so the case fell within section 6(d) and the intermediary was entitled to the benefit of Rule 8-A.
issues.legal_principle: Section 3 of the U.P. Agricultural Income-tax Act, 1948, charged the agricultural income of the previous year to tax, and section 2(13) defined that year by reference to the twelve months ending on June 30. Section 6(d) of the U.P. Zamindari Abolition and Land Reforms Act, 1951, covered tax on agricultural income for a period before vesting; Rule 8-A provided for its adjustment against compensation. The timing of assessment after the previous year did not alter the period to which the taxed income related. No earlier cases were relied on.

rule.if: agricultural_income_tax_adjustment_dispute and tax_is_charged_on_previous_year_income and previous_year_ended_before_vesting and assessment_was_made_after_vesting

predicates.agricultural_income_tax_adjustment_dispu: The matter concerns adjustment of agricultural income tax against compensation payable to a person whose estate vested in the State.
predicates.tax_is_charged_on_previous_year_income: The tax is imposed on agricultural income earned during a defined previous year.
predicates.previous_year_ended_before_vesting: The period in which the taxed income was earned ended before the estate vested in the State.
predicates.assessment_was_made_after_vesting: The tax assessment was made after the estate vested in the State.
predicates.tax_qualifies_for_adjustment_as_pre_vest: The tax is treated as relating to a period before vesting and is eligible for adjustment against compensation.

issues.definition: When agricultural income tax is imposed on income from a previous year that ended before vesting, it qualifies as pre-vesting dues even if assessed afterward.

issues.legal_issue: An appellate court should remand for factual determination when the record is insufficient to decide whether compensation remains available for the ordered tax adjustment.
material_facts: The High Court directed adjustment of tax against compensation on the assumption that compensation bonds remained to be delivered.
The revenue authorities argued in the appeal that compensation bonds had already been issued, but that contention had not been raised before the High Court.
The record did not provide sufficient material to determine whether compensation bonds remained to be delivered, and the Court declined to consider additional evidence at that stage.
issues.conclusion: The Supreme Court set aside the High Court’s order and remanded the matter for the High Court to determine whether compensation bonds remained to be delivered and, if not, whether adjustment could otherwise be made effective.
issues.legal_principle: The Court did not decide from the existing record whether compensation bonds had already been delivered or whether adjustment could otherwise be effected. It held that the factual issue should be determined by the High Court on the evidence on record or further evidence brought before it. No statutory provision or earlier case was relied on for this procedural determination.

predicates.appeal_from_order_directing_compensation: The matter is an appeal from an order directing adjustment of dues against compensation.
predicates.availability_of_compensation_is_disputed: A party disputes whether compensation remains available for the directed adjustment.
predicates.record_is_insufficient_to_determine_avai: The evidence before the appellate court is inadequate to determine whether compensation remains available or whether the adjustment can otherwise be made effective.
predicates.appellate_court_should_remand_for_factua: The appellate court should set aside the order and remand the matter for the lower court to determine the relevant facts.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges a compensation adjustment and the record cannot establish whether compensation is available, the appellate court should remand for that factual determination.
